text:
The Maple Leafs have not won in nine games (0-8-1), they have been outscored 37-18 in that stretch, and this is not a bad-luck slump: they have 44% of the expected goals over it (expected goals measure the quality of chances). Saturday was the cruelest version, a two-goal lead against Columbus that became a 4-3 loss. Auston Matthews called it "inexcusable," William Nylander called his giveaway on the tying goal a "dumb play," and a Daily Faceoff Toronto piece wondered whether the skid "may end Jim Hiller's tenure." Around all of it, the headlines have moved on to whether Matthews should be traded and how carefully the team is handling Nylander.

Anthony Stolarz gets the net, at .902 and roughly break-even against expected this season. Kirill Marchenko (lower body, 14 points in 14 games) is still out, though he is back at practice. John Tavares has moved up beside Nick Paul and Nylander and has goals in back-to-back games, and he returns to the building where his career began. Easton Cowan is playing about 20 minutes a night now, which is why he is one of our Sleepers. Aatu Raty, newly arrived, is excited for the chance despite the skid, per The Leafs Nation. Our numbers give Toronto a 2% playoff chance.

The Islanders have points in seven straight (4-0-3), and our numbers are skeptical: they have 47% of the expected goals and are +9 on goals against -7.9 on chances, which means Ilya Sorokin (11.2 goals saved above expected, .928 over his last five) is carrying a lot. Matthew Schaefer has 15 points in his last ten and 25 on the season, Simon Holmstrom a seven-game point streak, and Casey Cizikas just played his 1,000th game. Mathew Barzal gets more ice. "I think he's ready for more," Pete DeBoer said, per NHL.com's Stefen Rosner.
headline: Nine without a win, and the questions get louder
